clue.text: Hospital nurses register The War Cry

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the hospital word cradles the register word

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
a log is a written register or record

explanation.surface: A hospital nurse signs off on a copy of The War Cry, the Salvation Army's newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The War Cry' looks like a title, but only 'War Cry' defines; the word began as a Gaelic battle shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchphrase was originally a Highland clan's shout rallying fighters into battle.

clue.text: Saw red article boring children

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the article goes inside the word for children

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or children
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper when a piece of writing bored their children.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe being furious, boiling over with anger internally.

clue.text: Maybe monks will organise rule book

definitions.meaning: a religious community such as Benedictines is an example of this
to reserve or request goods, as in a shop

explanation.surface: Monks will put a book of rules in order.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covering a monastic brotherhood, arranging, commanding and placing a purchase request.

clue.text: Old area, nice ground saved by conservationists

indicators.note: the preceding letters are kept safe by the conservation body, which comes after them
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of nice are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the UK's heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A pleasant old patch of land has been rescued by a conservation charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns NICE into NCIE; the National Trust is a British body preserving historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something of great age, dating from long ago.

clue.text: To cure duke, queen brought in paper

indicators.note: the queen's letter is fetched inside the word for curing

parts.note: to heal is to cure
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: To treat an ailing duke, a queen was brought into a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common name for a newspaper, as in the Glasgow title.

clue.text: Animal determined to shed coat

indicators.note: the word determined loses its outer layers front and back, leaving the inner letters

explanation.surface: A creature is resolved to moult its fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip DET from the front and D from the back of 'determined'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat in its white winter fur is a mammal, so it is an animal.

clue.text: For doubters, head of audit worked out costings

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
worked out suggests the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Sceptical people get the chief auditor to calculate the costs.
explanation.definitionFit: People who hold that God's existence cannot be known are religious sceptics.

clue.text: Copier installed in dull clothing business

indicators.note: the copier word is fitted inside the word for dull

parts.note: dry means dull, as in a dry lecture
an aper is one who apes, or copies

explanation.surface: A photocopier was put in at a drab clothing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use the trade of a draper, selling cloth and garments, goes by this name.

clue.text: Play: diverting drama with anthems about knight

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the knight
diverting means turning aside, so the letters of drama and anthems are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An entertaining drama full of anthems is about a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverting' looks like praise for the drama, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This is George Bernard Shaw's 1894 comedy, whose title quotes Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Corner indefinite number engaged in plot

indicators.note: engaged means occupied within, so the number sits inside the plot word

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An unknown number of people are cornered while involved in a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve in a road can be called a corner.

clue.text: Coal miner in dispute with energy official

indicators.note: letters in dispute are at odds and thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A coal miner is arguing with a power company official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'official' looks like a noun, a person, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something done with formal ritual or state protocol.

clue.text: Attack burn, say, from the east

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: An assault involving burning, perhaps, comes from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush against the enemy, like the cavalry's, is an assault.

clue.text: Forbidding nun to ring home

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so the nun word goes round the home word

parts.note: a nun is called Sister
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A stern rule forbids a nun from telephoning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something threatening and ominous.

clue.text: Acknowledging hand in a racket with government

indicators.note: the hand word is placed inside the pair a and racket

parts.note: din is noise, a racket
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Someone is owning up to having a hand in a government swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean conceding or confessing that something is true.

clue.text: Found truck following popular small bird

indicators.note: the truck word comes after the others

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a tit is a small songbird
a ute is a utility truck, Australian slang

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a lorry tailing a well-loved little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find but is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to set up or establish something, such as a college.

clue.text: The Italian stops extremely lovely girl

indicators.note: stops means plugs up, so the Italian article sits in the gap
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: IL is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian man halts a thoroughly lovely girl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's first name, taken from the flower.

clue.text: Service entertainers, each holding poles

indicators.note: the each word grips the poles inside it

parts.note: N and S are the North and South poles

explanation.surface: Performers who entertain, each holding a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: ENSA, the Entertainments National Service Association, put on shows for British forces in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: The organisation was the troupe of performers entertaining British servicemen during the war.

clue.text: Sad English stage actor denied rise to tour India

indicators.note: touring round means surrounding, so the pair goes around India's letter

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: the word actor is denied, so loses, the rise word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or rise
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An unhappy English stage actor is refused a pay rise for an Indian tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reads as a pay rise but is a hill, a West Country tor; 'stage actor' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes mournful lament, as in a poem for the dead.

clue.text: Band's standing quota? No thank you

parts.note: status means standing or rank

indicators.note: no means without, so the thank-you word is removed from quota

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: A musical group's limit on its share is politely declined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is the definition: a British rock group famous for 'Rockin' All Over the World'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a long-running British rock group.

clue.text: Man's replacing one in newspaper plant

indicators.note: the man's word takes the place of one in the newspaper word

parts.note: a newspaper is often called a title
I is the Roman numeral one
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: A man's replacing someone in a newspaper factory.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a prickly weed, the emblem of Scotland, so a plant.

clue.text: Wanting leader, Merseyside town brings in one fabulous creature

indicators.note: the shortened town takes the numeral inside it
wanting means lacking, so the town loses its first letter

parts.note: Runcorn is a town in Cheshire on the Mersey estuary
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leaderless northern town is introducing a wonderful being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means from fable, not merely wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned horse is a creature of legend and fable.

clue.text: White paintings, for example, full of information

indicators.note: the paintings word is filled with the information word

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Bright white canvases are packed with data.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry this is the term for the tincture silver, depicted as white.

clue.text: Poke about in wee tree

indicators.note: the poke and about words go inside the wee word

parts.note: pee is urine, wee
to dig is to poke
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone prods around in a very small tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks Scottish for small; it is urine.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree shows line of descent, as does a recorded lineage.

clue.text: Current airline once covered Rhode Island peninsula

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the old airline wraps around the state abbreviation

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, now defunct
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A present-day carrier once flew over Rhode Island and a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current airline' suggests the Spanish carrier, but I is current and the airline is BEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the landmass holding Spain and Portugal, surrounded by sea on three sides.

clue.text: European trophies over bar

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the trophies word reads backwards

parts.note: pots is slang for trophies or cups

explanation.surface: European cups won are more than a pub can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the verb means to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Tale by lodger gripping snooty officer

indicators.note: the tale and lodger pair grips the snooty letter

parts.note: a lie is a tall tale
a tenant is a lodger
U means upper-class, hence posh or snooty

explanation.surface: A lodger tells a story about a stuck-up army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a junior commissioned military rank, so an officer.

clue.text: Excessively large puppet

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: An oversized marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone used by others is a stooge, a puppet.

clue.text: Tops summit in Cairngorms, then relaxes

indicators.note: the summit of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: A hiker reaches a peak in the Scottish Cairngorm mountains, then takes it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridges and summits of hills are also called crests or tops.

clue.text: Bairn grabbing potty means to hurt someone

indicators.note: the child word grabs the potty word inside it

parts.note: wean is Scots for a young child, a bairn
a po is a chamber pot or potty

explanation.surface: A Scottish toddler snatching a potty might hurt someone with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything used to injure, such as a gun or knife, is an instrument of harm.
